title: Clothes and getting dressed
intro: Spanish uses the singular where English often uses a plural: un pantalón is a pair of trousers. Clothes go on with ponerse and come off with quitarse, both reflexive.

entries.note: Singular and uncountable, so la ropa está sucia, never las ropas. Not rope — that is la cuerda.

ex.es: Guarda la ropa en el armario.
ex.en: Put the clothes away in the wardrobe.

entries.note: la camiseta is a T-shirt or vest.

ex.en: He's wearing a white shirt.

entries.note: Singular in Spanish. los pantalones is also heard and means the same thing.

ex.en: Those trousers are too big for you.

ex.es: Se compró un vestido para la boda.
ex.en: She bought a dress for the wedding.

ex.es: La falda es demasiado corta para la oficina.
ex.en: The skirt is too short for the office.

entries.note: la chaqueta is a jacket; el saco a suit jacket in Latin America.

ex.en: Put your coat on, it's cold.

entries.note: Also el jersey in Spain, el pulóver in the Southern Cone.

ex.en: She knitted the sweater herself.

entries.note: las zapatillas or los tenis are trainers; una zapatería is a shoe shop.

ex.en: These shoes are tight on me.

entries.note: las medias in much of Latin America, where it also covers tights.

ex.en: I can't find one of the socks.

entries.note: la gorra is a cap with a peak.

ex.en: He wears a hat because of the sun.
I was carrying it in my pocket.

entries.note: One word for the button on a shirt and the one on a machine.

ex.en: One of his buttons came off.

entries.note: The j is silent at the end in most speech: re-LÓ.

ex.en: They gave me a watch.

ex.es: El reloj de la plaza va atrasado.
ex.en: The clock in the square is slow.

entries.note: Reflexive, with the article rather than a possessive: se puso los zapatos.

ex.en: Put on something more formal.

entries.note: In Latin America sacarse is just as common.

ex.es: Quítate el abrigo, aquí hace calor.
ex.en: Take your coat off, it's warm in here.
I'll get dressed in five minutes.

entries.note: Built like gustar: the garment is the subject. Me queda bien is it fits me well.

ex.es: Ese color te queda muy bien.
ex.en: That colour really suits you.

entries.note: For shoes Spanish says el número, not la talla.

ex.en: Do you have a bigger size?
The shirt is clean now.

ex.es: No te sientes con las manos sucias.
ex.en: Don't sit down with dirty hands.
